symbols.name: vector length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries of a vector to which the normalized transform F_q applies.
symbols.quote: The letters $u$ and $v$ denote complex vectors, and $q$ is the length of such a vector, the number of its entries.

symbols.name: input vector
symbols.meaning: A complex vector whose length is set by the transform applied to it.
symbols.quote: The letters $u$ and $v$ denote complex vectors, and $q$ is the length of such a vector, the number of its entries.

symbols.name: second vector
symbols.meaning: A complex vector whose length is set by the transform applied to it.
symbols.quote: The letters $u$ and $v$ denote complex vectors, and $q$ is the length of such a vector, the number of its entries.

symbols.name: normalized transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform of length q.
symbols.quote: $F_q$ is the normalized discrete Fourier transform of length $q$: for $u$ it returns the vector $F_q u$ with entries

symbols.name: entry index
symbols.meaning: An index of an entry of a vector, running from 0 to q-1 in the sum defining F_q.
symbols.quote: The indices $j$ and $k$ run over the entries, taken modulo $q$.

symbols.name: output index
symbols.meaning: An index of an entry of a transformed vector, taken modulo q.
symbols.quote: The indices $j$ and $k$ run over the entries, taken modulo $q$.

symbols.name: coordinate permutation
symbols.meaning: A rearrangement of the entries of a vector.
symbols.quote: A coordinate permutation $\Pi$ rearranges the entries of a vector.

symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries of the source vectors, the length of the source axis.
symbols.quote: The integer $s$ is the length of the source axis and $t$ is the length of the target axis, with $s<t$ and $\gcd(s,t)=1$.

symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries of the target vectors, the length of the target axis.
symbols.quote: The integer $s$ is the length of the source axis and $t$ is the length of the target axis, with $s<t$ and $\gcd(s,t)=1$.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of length-s vectors given by (P_s u)_j = u_{tj}.
symbols.quote: The permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ reorder the entries of length-$s$ and length-$t$ vectors by $(P_s u)_j = u_{tj}$ and $(P_t v)_k = v_{-sk}$, and coprimality makes each map a bijection.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of length-t vectors given by (P_t v)_k = v_{-sk}.
symbols.quote: The permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ reorder the entries of length-$s$ and length-$t$ vectors by $(P_s u)_j = u_{tj}$ and $(P_t v)_k = v_{-sk}$, and coprimality makes each map a bijection.

symbols.name: precision
symbols.meaning: The precision, which fixes the grid 2^{-p} on which approximate values are stored.
symbols.quote: Here $p$ is the precision, which fixes the grid $2^{-p}$ of stored values, and $\alpha$ is a fixed integer parameter with $2 \le \alpha < p$.

symbols.name: integer parameter
symbols.meaning: A fixed integer parameter of the identity, with 2 <= alpha < p.
symbols.quote: Here $p$ is the precision, which fixes the grid $2^{-p}$ of stored values, and $\alpha$ is a fixed integer parameter with $2 \le \alpha < p$.

symbols.name: relative gap
symbols.meaning: The ratio t/s minus one, which measures how far apart the two lengths are.
symbols.quote: The number $\theta = t/s-1$ is the relative gap between $t$ and $s$, and the identity needs $\theta > p/\alpha^4$.

symbols.name: source map
symbols.meaning: A linear contraction from length-s vectors to length-t vectors.
symbols.quote: The maps $A$ and $B_0$ are linear contractions, with $A$ taking length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors and $B_0$ taking length-$t$ vectors to length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: target map
symbols.meaning: A linear contraction from length-t vectors to length-s vectors.
symbols.quote: The maps $A$ and $B_0$ are linear contractions, with $A$ taking length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors and $B_0$ taking length-$t$ vectors to length-$s$ vectors.

relations.quote: This identity computes its transforms by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md), which replaces a transform of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two.
